meta.note: Recorded output of the point, timeline and site-search functions before the data-source seam work. Regenerate only on purpose.

ephemeris.source: Truncated Meeus lunar theory + low-precision Sun + IAU lunar orientation (WGCCRE 2009); checked against JPL Horizons
ephemeris.note: Accuracy about 0.02 degrees; fine for visualising illumination and comms windows, not for mission-grade planning. Angles are relative to a smooth 1737.4 km sphere (no terrain).

terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA global DEM LDEM_64 (473.8 m/pixel), averaged into 0.25 degree map cells (pipeline v1, public/data/v1/manifest.json)
terrain.note: Height and slope are interpolated between map cells of 0.25 degrees (about 7.6 km); slope is the mean over a 474 m baseline inside the cell, not the slope at the exact point, so it is not a landing-safety slope. The horizon profile has 32 azimuths (11.25 degree steps), computed from the cell centre with rays up to 300 km on a spherical Moon, and interpolated between cells.

visibility.source: Sun/Earth ephemeris + terrain horizon profile (see provenance.terrain)
visibility.note: A disk counts as visible when its upper limb is above the terrain horizon at the azimuth of the disk centre. diskVisibleFraction treats the horizon as a straight line at that elevation (0 = fully hidden, 1 = fully visible). nextRiseUtc / nextSetUtc are searched up to 60 days ahead in 10 minute steps and refined to about 2 seconds; null means no change was found in that window.

yearStats.source: Sun/Earth ephemeris + terrain horizon profile, computed per request
yearStats.note: Hourly samples (8760 hours) from 2030-01-01T00:00:00Z, same visibility rule as provenance.visibility. Runs cut by the start or end of the period count with their cut length. bothVisibleFraction is the share of hours in which the Sun and the Earth are visible at the same time. One year is not the worst year: the Moon's orbit has an 18.6 year cycle that changes how far Sun and Earth swing above and below the horizon near the poles. The whole-Moon maps (L4-L7) use the same rule at the map cell centre, so they can differ slightly from this exact-point result.

conventions.longitude: selenographic degrees, east positive, normalized to [-180, 180]
conventions.azimuth: compass bearing in degrees: north = 0, increasing toward east
conventions.elevation: degrees above the local horizontal of a smooth sphere; 90 = zenith
conventions.height: meters above the 1737.4 km reference sphere

provenance.source: Sun/Earth ephemeris + terrain horizon profile from NASA LRO LOLA LDEM_64 (0.25 degree map cells, public/data/v1/manifest.json)
provenance.note: A disk counts as visible when its upper limb is above the terrain horizon at the azimuth of the disk centre (same rule as get_point_conditions). Window start and end times are refined to about 2 seconds; a window shorter than 10 minutes (rising and setting between two checks) can be missed. Sun and Earth positions are accurate to about 0.02 degrees, not mission-grade. Horizon is the map cell horizon (about 7.6 km cells), not the exact point.

One year is not the worst year (18.6 year lunar orbit cycle). Not mission-grade.
